pr_body:
fix #2009
fix #5270

### Description

Makes built apps portable when using relative base (`base: './'` or `base: ''`).

When using a relative base, there shouldn't be any absolute URL. Including paths to public files and paths to assets from HTML files.

Related discussions:
- https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions/7611#discussioncomment-2500939
- https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/issues/595

Why we need relative base support, from @Rich-Harris's comment:
> - the basepath is configured by an environment variable at runtime
> - the site is deployed with IPFS
> - you're building a Chrome extension
> - the site is being viewed on something like the Internet Archive

### Update to modern browser targets

> Edit: We discussed this in a team meeting and we have agreed to update the browser targets as described here in v3 

We need support for `import.meta.url` to be able to find the assets URL in some cases (for the preload URLs for example). 

[`import.meta` is at 91.22%](https://caniuse.com/?search=import.meta), and we are currently require [`dynamic import support` so we are at 91.47%](https://caniuse.com/es6-module-dynamic-import). Given that `import.meta.url` will enable us to implement features like this PR, and the numbers will keep getting better, I think we could change our default modern target in Vite v3 and push an extra 0.25% of users to legacy mode. See Discussion with @bluwy and @sapphi-red in Discord [here](https://discord.com/channels/804011606160703521/804439875226173480/961231593278689321)

The new esbuild resolved target upgrades `'es2019'` to `'es2020'` and downgrades safari from `13.1` to `13` so we keep transpiling nullish coallesing (still at ~89%)
 
```js
resolved.target = [
  'es2020', // support import.meta.url
  'edge88',
  'firefox78',
  'chrome87',
  'safari13' // transpile nullish coallesing
]
```

`@vitejs/plugin-legacy` is updated to check `import.meta` support (on top of dynamic import support):
```js
const detectModernBrowserCode = `try{import(new URL(import.meta.url).href).catch(()=>1);}catch(e){}window.${detectModernBrowserVarName}=true;`
```

### Asset URLs replacements in JS files

Edit: after a discussion with @bluwy, he proposed we keep using quotes and `JSON.stringify` and interpolate using `" + ... + "`.

### Alternative interpolation strategy that is no longer used in the PR

For assets paths imported from a JS file, or for CSS inlined with asset URLs, we need to use `import.meta.url` to obtain a runtime absolute path because these strings can be re-exported and used in other files, or used directly in the DOM.
     
Instead of plain strings 
```js
return `export default ${JSON.stringify(css)}`
```

We could use template literals in these cases
```js
// Return a template string so we can use interpolation when replacing __VITE_ASSET__
return `export default \`${css}\``
```

Allowing us to inject runtime interpolation with `new URL(...,import.meta.url)`
```js
const replacement = isRelativeBase(config.base)
  ? `\${new URL(${JSON.stringify(outputFilepath)},import.meta.url)}`
  : outputFilepath
s.overwrite(match.index, match.index + full.length, replacement, {
  contentOnly: true
})
```

### Note

During the Vite 2.0.0 beta, https://github.com/vitejs/vite/commit/00bc4466567bd5613d67abd1bdf46d9c9cb23a80 added relative base support, fixing https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/1669. Afterward, tests for relative base weren't included in Vite's CI. So the code evolved and we lost support for this feature.

---

### What is the purpose of this pull request? <!-- (put an "X" next to an item) -->

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New Feature
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Other
pr_comments:
Tests are passing, except for Windows. We are probably missing a path normalization.

More testing is still needed, I changed some playgrounds to use relative base, and tested by hand in some others (there is a new `build:portable` script in the assets playground for example). It isn't easy to test a playground with both bases without doubling the time and making the expectation more complex. So maybe some playgrounds using relative base, a new `portable` playground for some specific checks, and adding the `build:portable`, `preview:portable` to most playgrounds for manual debugging could be enough.

Looks like tests are failing because this line is missing `normalizePath`. (I have not checked all the code but at least it worked for playground/vue and playground/worker)
https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/c02537b5b2ac5e39313601cc22530ef6201239b9/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/workerImportMetaUrl.ts#L162

In addition, I think this PR will fix #5270 and #7279 since `import.meta` won't be transpiled.

I don't know how disruptive it could be for the ecosystem, but relative paths seem like a better default to me than `base: '/'`. I think users could even open a built app from the filesystem without needing a local preview server 🤔
Should we analyze changing the default base in Vite 3.0? For sure we would need a major, we would need to wait if not another year.

Note: Right now, during dev even if the user sets `base: './'`, Vite will cheat and use `'/'` that makes some handling easier in the dev server. I think this is fine, I'm thinking if we could still try to use relative base during dev as much as possible so Dev and Build are closer but I don't know if the extra complexity is justified.

Posting my reply in the Discord channel here for a more public discussion:

The relative base path doesn't work well for code-splitting. That's why webpack introduced `publicPath: 'auto'` even though `./` already works. https://github.com/webpack/webpack/issues/11127 (`./` is relative to the page URL, `auto` is relative to the script URL, i.e. `import.meta.url`, which may be a CDN URL)

Note that even if we follow the webpack approach, the `auto` public path has some edge cases in legacy browsers that cannot be fully resolved:
Webpack recommends falling back to `currentScript` in legacy bundles, but it's not equivalent to `import.meta.url` in functionality. It will fail in callbacks or event handlers.
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/currentScript
> It's important to note that this will not reference the `<script>` element if the code in the script is being called as a callback or event handler; it will only reference the element while it's initially being processed.

I think what this PR is doing for `'./'` is similar to Webpack's `publicPath: 'auto'`, as it is using `import.meta.url` as you describe. 

I like having a `base: 'auto'`, it is more clear than `'./'` or `''` because that isn't the base used all the time. For simplicity, we could make all of them work in the same way, since `'./'` is the same as `'auto'` in the cases where it works. Maybe we could add a warning when the user uses `'./'` or `''` deprecating them and pointing to the new `'auto'` instead.

> @benmccann would you be able to review this PR and check if most use cases discussed in https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/issues/595 (or involve others from the Svelte community that may be interested in helping push this change forward?)

@Rich-Harris might be the best person to take a look at this one. I see @dominikg and @bluwy have both taken a look at this PR as well though

Funny enough, we've been discussing moving the opposite direction in Astro, towards root-level URL path references. The main reason was that statically generated 404 pages are common (supported in Netlify/Vercel/others via a `/404.html` page). Because these can be served from anywhere, any relative URL references will break.

I assume this change will break most 404 pages served this way?

Our current workaround is for users to put something like `<base href="/404">` in their 404 template. Maybe we could automate this on our end, so this isn't a blocker for Astro necessarily.

> Funny enough, we've been discussing moving the opposite direction in Astro, towards root-level URL path references. The main reason was that statically generated 404 pages are common (supported in Netlify/Vercel/others via a `/404.html` page). Because these can be served from anywhere, any relative URL references will break.
> 
> I assume this change will break most 404 pages served this way?

This change only applies when users will use a relative base (`base: './'`). But even if they use a relative base, I think that this PR shouldn't affect your use case. It would be great to have a reproduction if there is an issue so I can test it.

There are [good use cases](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions/7611#discussioncomment-2500939) for supporting all paths be relative (it is important that all are properly transformed, both absolute and relative paths in user code). I wonder if it isn't a better default for Vite, but I don't think this will be changed in v3.

Ah gotcha, glad that this doesn't break that use-case for now. 

Separate from Astro, it does still sound like this feature would break a `404.html` page when built with Vite + a relative base value: https://vitejs.dev/guide/build.html#multi-page-app

We started discussing the PR in a team meeting, we have agreed to update the browser targets as described in Vite v3. So the PR is unblocked, but we still need to review the implementation more closely.
After a discussion with @bluwy, he proposed we keep using quotes and `JSON.stringify`, interpolating using `" + ... + "` for asset URLs replacements in JS files.

@DreierF @cawa-93 we're reworking how relative base work so every asset is made relative or dynamically absolute using `import.meta.url`. Since you asked for this feature in https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/1669, would you check that this PR works in your projects if you have some time? @DreierF you were using `base: ''`, while others used `base: './'`. I can't understand the difference between these two, this PR at this point makes both of them work in the same way. Are these equivalent in your setups?
@distantnative would you test if this PR fixes [your issue](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/7766#issuecomment-1122776973) with module preload relative paths?

In the meantime we also switched to using `base: './'`, but can't quite remember why. From my perspective they should indeed be equivalent. I'll try to find some time in the coming days to give it a try.
@patak-dev Everything seems to be working. I did not notice any destructive changes

Gave it a try now in dev and prod, deployed with and without URL prefixes (at deploy time) and didn't notice any issues.
Great work!
Thanks for testing @cawa-93 and @DreierF!

We had conflicts in the way we handle worker URLs after we merged:
- https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/7804

Workers are no longer injecting a `__VITE_ASSET_{...}__` placeholder. But the refactoring was interesting because now we are no longer going to get:
```js
export default new Worker("" + new URL(...) + "", { ... })
```
But instead generate:
```js
export default new Worker(new URL(...), { ... })
```
See https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/7644/files#diff-3b7bb11b5633d82f82c069037789e105005d657667b1da1e96c18fcf3eb622adR243, and also here https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/7644/files#diff-30eb02919cdc99946edccdc1854b56b09fa4d784bd2ed9de30f5f9182bb6a6d9R158

We are also now forcing a `JSON.stringify(url).slice(1,-1)` that isn't bad here (I think it wasn't a bug because it was encoded, still I think it is safer): https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/7644/files#diff-91776e7c6039d23a070162f02a69cd46046a2095bd5ecb384ae9e27f2ea5288fR103

@poyoho @bluwy would you re-review these changes?

I'm testing this out with SvelteKit, and running into some problems. As far as I can tell, `__vitePreload` is creating links that are relative to the document, rather than relative to the _module_, resulting in incorrect URLs.

Have I misunderstood how this works?

@Rich-Harris yes, exactly! I was also testing, you got there first. The problem is the custom `assetFileNames` and `entryFileNames`. We need to know the relative path from the chunks to the assets, so the PR was bailing out to the old scheme if there were custom asset file names before https://github.com/vitejs/vite/commit/9681acabdd75dda2fcd8798ee2becc57b63544ab. 

I think we have two options:
- We can force `assetFileNames` and `entryFileNames` being siblings.
- Or, we derive the assetDir and entryDir from these, and we compute the relative path between them and allow the user to use different folders.

I'll try to implement the second one, and if not, I think making these folders siblings is a small price to pay :)

Hi @patak-dev thanks for this initiative!

I just tested with my svelte-kit template and have issue with relative path, the CSS does not load for example.

You can see it work on the root domain : https://jolly-roger-git-vite-relative-base-wighawag.vercel.app/

but fails when loading as a folder on ipfs gateway :  https://ipfs.io/ipfs/QmP3RRYQt4jDrZPL22pkmrqdhX2oyftFwPyH4QqvtGgAZu/


I also get this error/warning in the console while building : 

```
build_service_worker: The value for kit.vite.base specified in svelte.config.js has been ignored. This option is controlled by SvelteKit.
```

See repo branch : https://github.com/wighawag/jolly-roger/tree/vite-relative-base

It is a monorepo and you can run the web app against an ipfs gateway emulator via `pnpm web:build:serve staging`

I am not sure if there is anything I need to set in the svelte.config file though ?

(I am using adapter-static for the test)

By the way, might be useful for testing (it is for me) I use my package [ipfs-gateway-emulator](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ipfs-gateway-emulator) which emulates ipfs gateway and allow you to access the same website via `localhost:8080` and `localhost:8080/ipfs/<whatever>/` (And when accessed by the later, request to the root fails (using referer))

Which allow to test relative path easily

@wighawag I don't think that SvelteKit is ready for relative base yet. Would it be possible for you to try some IPFS use cases using plain Vite so we can be sure that core is capable enough to handle them? @bluwy is my assumption right that adding `base: './'` to SvelteKit would not work yet? I'm seeing a lot of absolute paths in the generated HTML that shouldn't be there. IIUC, SvelteKit has its own HTML middleware). There are quite a few changes in our HTML middleware to properly handle relative paths that would need to be replicated in SvelteKit.

I think we should be good for reviewing the PR again. There were [several assumptions regarding output dist structure](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/7644#issuecomment-1126252762) that have now been removed. Custom `assetFileNames` et al should work (including the functional form).

For relative base. When a CSS asset is generated, all public and normal asset paths should be relative to the generated asset filename. The bit I'm not so sure about is to use a dummy call to `assetFileNames` in case it is a function, but I think it should work fine.
When a JS chunk is generated, public and asset paths should be absolute (as these URL strings could be injected into any HTML, or exported to other modules). So we compute the relative path from the generated JS chunk to the asset and wrap it into `new URL(..., import.meta.url)`.
Worker chunks could also potentially be generated in different folders from the app chunks, so we also need to do the same for them (see `__VITE_WORKER_ASSET__`)

Public assets paths generation is now delayed in the same way as regular assets (see `__VITE_PUBLIC_ASSET__`) because we need to know the filename where they are going to end up.

I added test cases here [test: add relative base asset test cases](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/7644/commits/7ee53f60fea5d5ae406e4abf45709a52afcde07e). These are almost all the tests from the normal `assets` playground but using relative base and custom `entryFileNames`, `chunkFileNames`, and `assetFileNames`. There are subtle diffs in most tests, we could abstract a common test case generator for both absolute and relative base but I don't know if we'll end up with something simpler. I think duplication is ok here. We should also add some test cases for workers with relative base.

Note: I needed to change the `playground/assets/nested/テスト-測試-white space.png` content because it was the same as `playground/assets/nested/icon.png` before and if I configured `build.assetsInlineLimit: 0` there is a bug. I'll create an issue later about this, it is unrelated to the PR.

> @bluwy is my assumption right that adding `base: './'` to SvelteKit would not work yet? I'm seeing a lot of absolute paths in the generated HTML that shouldn't be there.

Judging from [SvelteKit's code here](https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/blob/70f830c23355d0e20d5b2e9b2eafb8a5002d3bf8/packages/kit/src/core/build/index.js#L33-L37), it's forcing a root base by default to workaround some previous issues. So when this PR is merged it should directly address the TODO, which SvelteKit can adopt. I'm not sure if there's more behind relative base other than that though.

Confirmed that this now works for a SvelteKit test case, the only change needed being to change `base` in our internal config to `./`. Wonderful work, thank you so much @patak-dev! Can't wait to use this 😍

We already discussed with the team and approved changing the modern browser targets increasing the baseline to browsers supporting `import.meta.url` (that would be useful moving forward not only for this PR). The implementation got a few reviews in the past few days (see reviews invalidated by added test cases and minor fixes in the last commits). And we now have success stories from SvelteKit and partial testing also from Nuxt (@danielroe was also testing it yesterday).

Let's merge the PR so we can start building on top of it. There are changes I think would be good to make but it will be easier to discuss them in separate PRs. It is also better if we can later release a new v3 alpha patch with it so we start getting more testing from the ecosystem.
Thanks to the folks that tested along the way, please create issues from now on so we can stabilize things for v3. @wighawag I'm especially interested in your use case as it will be a big stress test for these changes.
Released as part of vite@3.0.0-alpha.1

Hi there! I Thank you for this amazing project. 

After a lot of fiddling around with the `base` option, I found, that in my setup, it would also make sense to use `import.meta.url` instead of the current browser URL, if it was set to `./`. Intuitively, I would expect that links to assets (js `import` or css `url()`) would resolve relative to their respective _referencing file_, not relative to whatever my website's current URL is. Here's my project tree (It's a classic PHP website, the setup is loosely following the [approach described here](https://sebastiandedeyne.com/vite-with-laravel/)):

```shell
.
├── index.php
└── subfolder
   ├── assets # my equivalent of 'dist' folder
   ├── assets-src # my equivalent of default 'src' folder
   ├── composer.json
   ├── composer.lock
   ├── lib
   ├── node_modules
   ├── package-lock.json
   ├── package.json
   └── vite.config.js
```

My `vite.config.js` looks like this:

```js
import { resolve } from 'path';

import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import liveReload from 'vite-plugin-live-reload'

export default defineConfig(({ command, mode }) => {
  return {
    base: './', // resolves correctly for css assets when being built. doesn't resolve in either scenarios for js import statements
    build: {
      target: 'es2015',
      outDir: 'assets',
      rollupOptions: {
        input: {
          frontend: 'assets-src/frontend.js',
          admin: 'assets-src/admin.js'
        },
        output: {
          entryFileNames: `[name].js`,
          chunkFileNames: `[name].js`,
          assetFileNames: `[name].[ext]`
        }
      },
    },
    server: {
      host: 'vite-with-backend.test',
      port: 3000,
      strictPort: true
    },
})
```
I was able to solve this by using an absolute path as `base` in different contexts, like this:

```js
const basePath = __dirname.split('/wwwroot')[1]; // wwwroot is the very root folder
base: command === 'serve' ? basePath : `${basePath}/assets/`,
```
...but I often have the scenario that my local development path is different to the path in production (e.g. when I install a website on the remote server inside a sub-directory, but my local site is running in the root).

My suggested solution would be to detect if `base` is set to `./`, and if so, replace it like this:
```js
let base = "./";
if( base === "./" ) base = new URL(import.meta.url).pathname.replace(/\/[^\/]+$/, '/');
```
